content:
For a candidate maximum time \(M\), elf \(E_j\) can deliver to house \(i\) only if
\[
ij \le M \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i \le \left\lfloor \frac Mj\right\rfloor.
\]
The bounds \(\left\lfloor M/j\right\rfloor\) are nonincreasing in \(j\). For a perfect matching to exist, the \(k\)-th smallest bound must be at least \(k\). This gives
\[
\left\lfloor \frac Mj \right\rfloor \ge 64-j \quad \text{for all } j=1,\dots,63,
\]
so
\[
M \ge j(64-j).
\]
The maximum of \(j(64-j)\) occurs at \(j=32\), giving
\[
M \ge 32\cdot 32 = 1024.
\]
This is achievable by assigning elf \(E_j\) to house \(64-j\), since
\[
j(64-j) \le 1024.
\]
Thus the minimum completion time is
\[
\boxed{1024}
\]
